Phone (4b) emulation and its lighting test are only available on Phone (4a) or Phone (4b).

While enabled, the whole app uses the Phone (4b) profile. Visualizer modes and meter previews use four Glyphs, mapped to Phone (4a) physical channels 2–5. Enabling the recording light adds physical channel 6 as the fifth Glyph.
Stop the visualizer before changing this setting.
Enable Phone (4b) emulation above to use the Phone (4b) lighting test on this Phone (4a).
Emulated output: Phone (4b) A1–A4 → Phone (4a) physical channels 2–5; recording → channel 6.
Direct Phone (4b) output: A1–A4 → physical channels 0–3; recording → experimental channel 4.
How to use the lighting test

1. Stop the visualizer. 2. Tap A1–A4 to check each white Glyph. 3. Tap Recording to check the recording light. “All four” tests the normal frame; “All + recording” tests the optional five-light frame.

To light up the Glyph, you need to enable Glyph Interface debug mode.\nPressing the enable button will try to turn it on automatically. Shizuku or Sui is required.
This action requires Shizuku to be running. Start Shizuku or Sui, grant permission to this app, and then try again.

On Phone (1), you need to enable Glyph Interface debug mode to use Glyph Lights.\nBy Nothing\'s design, it automatically turns off again after 48 hours.\nInstall Shizuku and enable it from this app, or use the ADB command below to enable it manually.
adb shell settings put global nt_glyph_interface_debug_enable 1
Automatically runs the Glyph Interface debug enable command on start.\nShizuku or Sui is required.
